digest.intro: Microfabrication goes open-source, gold flows east, and coral heals by touch.

items.title: Trump Signs Direct Diesel Deal with Russia — The Architecture of a Pivot
items.blurb: On October 9th, Trump invoked OFAC General License 135 to authorize 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel immediately, scaling to 3 million by April — while the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed after seven months of US-Iran conflict. The analysis is genuinely multi-paradigm: realist supply shock logic colliding with the normative wreckage of half a decade of sanctions architecture. The short version: material pressure won over alliance coherence, and Europe is now watching its isolation strategy dissolve from the inside.

items.title: Gold Is Now America's Top Export — And Nobody Has an Official Explanation
items.blurb: Since October 2025, gold has beaten oil, pharmaceuticals, and aircraft to become the highest-value US export almost every single month — and February 2026 may have set an all-time tonnage record. The flow is routing through Switzerland's refiners, then to Hong Kong (read: China), then London. No official explanation exists, but the signal is legible: foreign sovereigns are quietly swapping dollar reserves for metal, and the US mining and recycling base is the seller of last resort.

sections.heading: DIY Microfabrication Is Having Its RepRap Moment

items.title: RepRapMicron PIKA v0.02 — Open Source Sub-Micron 3D Printing
items.blurb: The RepRap community has printed a 0.5mm Benchy at 4μm layer height — and PIKA v0.02 is now achieving repeatable 1μm positioning within an 8mm cubic volume, depositing UV resin droplets as small as 4μm using a probe the machine etched itself. That last part is the tell: the tool making the tool. This is the exact trajectory FDM took in 2008, now aimed at MEMS-scale fabrication that currently requires cleanrooms.

items.title: Open MicroManipulator — Sub-Micrometer Motion Control for Under $500
items.blurb: A parallel-kinematic XYZ stage using off-the-shelf stepper motors and a 'magnetic gearing' trick that multiplies encoder resolution by 30x — achieving 50nm step resolution via G-code over USB serial. It pairs naturally with the RepRapMicron project and together they suggest a genuine convergence: the infrastructure for desktop microfabrication is being assembled in public, piece by piece, right now.

items.title: Bleached Coral Recovers in Days — Just by Touching a Healthy Neighbor
items.blurb: A lab accident led to the discovery: Stephen Palumbi noticed two coral fragments accidentally in contact, and where bleached met healthy, color returned. Controlled experiments confirmed full reversal of bleaching within days of physical contact — the symbiotic algae (Symbiodiniaceae) appear to transfer through direct touch, though the exact signaling mechanism is still being worked out. The finding is preliminary and lab-scale, but it's the first time fast, full reversal has been demonstrated and it reframes what recovery might look like at the reef level.

sections.heading: How Things Get Made and Owned

items.title: Meta's New TOS Quietly Claims Scraping Rights Over Everything You Link To
items.blurb: As of October 30, Meta's updated commercial terms will require any business account to grant Meta the right to crawl all domains and URLs associated with their products — no opt-out, just stop using Meta services if you disagree. Legal experts note this is structured to preempt the licensing battles news organizations are currently fighting with OpenAI: by getting consent baked into TOS, Meta sidesteps fair use entirely. If you have a studio website linked to an Instagram account, read this before the 30th.

items.title: Furifont — Pronunciation Built Into the Letterform Itself
items.blurb: Furigana — the small phonetic guides printed above Japanese kanji — normally require a separate annotation layer in HTML or typesetting. Furifont collapses this into the glyph itself: the pronunciation is part of the character, requiring no markup. It's a small, obsessive solution to a real problem, and it's worth five minutes of your time as a typographic idea about what a 'character' can contain.

facts.fact: PIKA v0.02 used a probe it etched itself to deposit UV resin droplets as small as 4μm — the machine is manufacturing its own tools at micron scale.
In February 2026, the US may have exported a record tonnage of gold in a single month — surpassing oil, aircraft, and pharmaceuticals in value almost every month since October 2025.
Trump's Russian diesel deal was authorized by a single Treasury instrument — OFAC General License 135 — circumventing years of multilateral sanctions architecture with one executive action.
NBA 2K25, released September 2025, is scheduled to become completely unplayable by December 31 of the same year due to server shutdowns — the proximate cause for the new 'Power to Players Act.'
A coral fragment in a lab fully reversed bleaching within days simply by being placed in physical contact with a healthy neighbor — the symbiotic algae appeared to transfer through touch alone.

make_something.prompt: Build a minimal XY plotter from two cheap steppers and a pen — not to draw, but to explore the gap between commanded position and actual position. Log the deviation at each point and render it as a field of error vectors. The map of where your machine lies is more interesting than anything it draws cleanly. This is the RepRapMicron problem at human scale: resolution vs. accuracy, and what the machine admits about itself.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film built like a feedback loop: memory, ritual, and the invisible systems Japan and Guinea-Bissau use to organize meaning. Marker treats the camera as a philosophical instrument, not a documentary one — every frame is a proposition about how images construct reality.

art_picks.title: One Year Performance (Time Clock Piece)
art_picks.creator: Tehching Hsieh
art_picks.why: Hsieh punched a time clock every hour for an entire year, photographing each moment — turning obsessive systems-adherence into the artwork itself. The kind of unreasonably deep commitment that makes you rethink what a body of work even means.

art_picks.title: Cluster / Passing
art_picks.creator: Félicia Atkinson
art_picks.why: Generative ambient built from field recordings, text, and sculptural sound — music that functions more like a spatial drawing than a song. Her albums resist resolution the way a good painting resists a single reading.

events.name: Walter De Maria: 360˚ I Ching / 64 Sculptures
events.why: 64 stainless steel rods arranged according to I Ching hexagrams — chance operations made permanent and physical; pair it with the Yang show in one Beacon day-trip.

events.name: Haegue Yang: Through
events.why: Yang's largest US commission spans both levels of the building — venetian blinds, metal louvers, bells, and bulbs organized by East Asian Five Phases theory and the music of exiled composer Isang Yun, making the architecture itself an oscillating score.

events.name: JPEGMAFIA – The Experimental Rap Tour
events.why: JPEGMAFIA makes albums like generative systems — samples, noise, and internet-culture detritus assembled into something that sounds alien and specific at once; live, it's confrontational in the best way.

events.name: Marc Ribot Quartet: Hurry Red Telephone (Album Release)
events.why: Ribot's guitar has always lived where noise, jazz, and political fury overlap — an album-release show at Roulette means the new material is fresh and the room is right.

events.name: Contemporaneous / Recap / Mantra: Seeing in the Dark
events.why: Three new works by Brendon Randall-Myers, Lila Meretzky, and Paul Pinto performed by three ensembles — experimental composition at Roulette, the city's best room for this, on a single high-stakes bill.

trial_sources.name: Chartbook by Adam Tooze
trial_sources.why: Columbia historian whose data-rich synthesis of geopolitics, economics, and history is the source other serious writers cite first when the news gets confusing.

trial_sources.name: Garbage Day by Ryan Broderick
trial_sources.why: The sharpest weekly anthropology of internet culture, meme velocity, and platform behavior — exactly the lens this reader needs for cultural transmission, youth identity, and how aesthetics spread.

trial_sources.name: House of Couture by Peptide Queen
trial_sources.why: A 25-year pharma and FDA regulatory insider writing credibly on peptide science, longevity protocols, and cellular senescence — practitioner knowledge over influencer hype.
